subject: Recap & next steps — FastBank parallel connections, streaming behavior, and rate caps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@fastbank.io>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@fastbank.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — FastBank parallel connections, streaming behavior, and rate caps

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we can align the SLO/quotas conversation with the engineering and procurement teams. I’ve attached a short SLO worksheet and our current ratecard PDF to make the numbers concrete.

Key items we heard on the call: 
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for short responses (<= 128 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state ~150 requests/sec across peak region (east-us), burst up to ~600 req/s for 5–10s.
- Concurrency: ~200 parallel in-flight requests (many are short), plus ~30 long-lived streaming WS connections for transcription workflows (avg 30s each).
- Average request size: 60 input tokens, 80 output tokens (we estimate ~140 tokens per call).
- Authentication & network: FastBank will run in our hosted environment for the pilot, likely move to Dedicated if traffic is sustained.

Questions we need from you to finalize a preliminary quota offer: 
1) Can you confirm the expected sustained QPS vs peak burst profile per region (east-us vs eu-west)?
2) For the streaming flows — are those bi-directional websockets or unidirectional server-sent events? Do you expect message multiplexing on the same socket?
3) Any hard limits on p99 latency we should be aware of for SLAs?
4) Token budgeting — will there be batched/coalesced requests (e.g., 5 user messages batched into one model call) or strictly single-user calls?

Proposed next steps (internal + external):
- I’ll draft a pilot quota proposal (reserved concurrency + burst window + streaming socket allotment) and share by EOD Pacific.
- Ben / Aditya, I’ve CC’d you for early pricing and capacity options — please suggest a 30-day pilot offer that includes credits for SLO verification.
- Arjun / Emily, please send any network egress constraints or procurement timelines so we can sync on procurement terms.

Attachments: SLO_worksheet.csv (short table to fill), redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@fastbank.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@fastbank.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — FastBank parallel connections, streaming behavior, and rate caps

Thanks Stephanie — this matches our notes. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Sustained QPS vs peak burst profile per region
We expect: east-us sustained 140–170 req/s (weekday peak 9–11am ET), burst to ~600 req/s for up to 15s during market open events. EU load is secondary (20–30 req/s sustained).

> 2) Streaming flows — WS vs SSE / multiplexing
Streaming is bi-directional WebSocket. We will multiplex multiple logical streams over a single socket only for mobile clients; server backends will use 1:1 sockets. Plan: 30 client sockets from user devices + up to 10 backend aggregator sockets that may multiplex.

> 3) Any hard limits on p99 latency for SLAs
We can tolerate p99 up to 450ms for short responses, but anything above 1s triggers escalation for customer-facing experiences.

> 4) Token budgeting — batched requests?
No batching for the initial pilot; requests are per-user. We can revisit batching in month 2.

Procurement note: Procurement expects a 45-day review period and needs a draft rate sheet and pilot SO to start internal approvals.

Arjun
Arjun Mehta
Head of Integrations | FastBank
arjun.mehta@fastbank.io
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@fastbank.io>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — FastBank parallel connections, streaming behavior, and rate caps

Looping in pricing/capacity thoughts based on the numbers Stephanie/Arjun laid out. Initial proposal to enable a low-friction pilot: 
- Pilot duration: 30 days.
- Reserved baseline: 200 concurrent short requests (to cover steady-state + headroom) and 40 streaming sockets (to cover backend + mobile multiplexing).
- Burst window: allow token-based burst up to 700 req/s for 20s (throttled by sliding-window) with automatic fallback to 200 req/s when capacity exhausted.
- Pricing: discounted pilot rate (35% off published ratecard) and $10k platform credit for SLO verification + 1 free week of dedicated capacity testing if they want to exercise Dedicated environment for latency validation.
- SLA: target p95 200ms in-host, p99 best-effort; for enterprise SLA we'd move to Dedicated and commit to p99 < 600ms with financial recourse (requires procurement signoff).

Operational notes: we’ll configure connection pooling on the FastBank integration endpoint with keep-alive 90s and per-IP socket caps; prefix caching should reduce token spend for repeated prompts. For the streaming multiplexing case, recommend we reserve additional ephemeral socket headroom (we can model 10% multiplex ratio on the 40 sockets).

Next actions (internal): 
- Aditya, run a quick capacity simulation for 200 concurrent short requests with the given token profile (140 tokens per call) and estimate GPU vCPU footprint + cost.
- Stephanie, I’ll draft the pilot rate sheet and a 1-page technical addendum for procurement.

Ben

Head of Customer Growth | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — appreciate the quick clarifications. Consolidating next steps and owners so we have a single cadence: 

External (FastBank):
- Arjun/Emily: confirm procurement timeline and any security checklist items we should pre-fill (Arjun mentioned 45 days). Please add answers to the SLO_worksheet.csv in the Drive link by next Tue.

Redwood actions:
- Ben: draft the 30-day pilot rate sheet + technical addendum and share to HubSpot + Drive (target: Mon EOD).
- Aditya: capacity sim and cost estimate for 200 concurrent short requests and 40 streaming sockets (target: Mon noon).
- Stephanie: I’ll prepare a pilot SLA summary, a stub SoW for procurement, and a short test plan for streaming latencies (target: Mon EOD).

Operational checklist for the pilot (high level):
- Reserve pilot quotas: concurrency baseline 200, streaming sockets 40, burst window up to 700 req/s configurable.
- Configure connection pooling with keep-alive 90s and sticky routing for aggregator sockets.
- Instrument token-level cost/tracing and a small eval set to detect quality regressions.

I’ve uploaded the SLO_worksheet.csv and the redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf to the Drive link above. Will also post the draft rate sheet to HubSpot and tag the FastBank company record (see related links).

If no objections, I’ll send a single thread to procurement with the pilot SoW + draft rate sheet on Monday to kick off the 45-day review.

Thanks — talk soon.
Stephanie
